title: Nightshift theme bridge: harmonize tokens for charts, tables, and elevated components
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our current dark-mode token layers diverge across surface components (buttons, tables, charts). This causes visual inconsistency when customers apply brand themes or deep-dark modes: chart axes, tooltip backgrounds, table zebra stripes, and elevated buttons use different contrast heuristics and token families, resulting in perceived flicker during theme toggles and incorrect focus states. Goal: Introduce a small compatibility layer ("Nightshift theme bridge") that centralizes mappings from brand and adaptive tokens into a unified set consumed by charts, tables, and elevated components. The bridge should: 1) maintain existing brand color intent, 2) avoid regressions for shallow dark themes, 3) reduce token surface-area for engineering by exposing a stable token subset for visualization components, and 4) allow per-brand overrides without duplicating tokens for each component.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens documented with concrete examples for 3 theme levels: light, neutral-dark, deep-dark
Charts render with unified axis, grid, and tooltip tokens in both brand and deep-dark themes (visual QA pass)
Table components (row hover, zebra stripes, header) reference bridge tokens and pass contrast checks (WCAG AA for text in header and row actions)
Buttons with elevation and outline variants use bridge tokens for shadow surfaces and hover states; visual snapshot tests added to storybook
tasks: Audit existing tokens used by charts, tables, buttons: produce CSV mapping component -> token -> usage

Design token bridge v1: propose 12 canonical bridge tokens (surface, elevated-surface, muted-text, strong-text, interactive, interactive-hover, divider, emphasis, tooltip-bg, tooltip-text, grid-line, axis-text)
Create Figma components for charts/tables using bridge tokens and run designer review
Add token aliases in token config (tokens.json) and create migration guide for frontend engineers
Partner with frontend to add storybook stories covering brand themes + deep-dark and add Percy snapshots
Roll out canary: apply to /console/datasets and /console/insights as smoke pages and run customer-facing QA
design_assets: Figma: Nightshift Theme Bridge (file link) - frames: Token map, Charts examples, Table examples
engineering_notes: Prefer alias-based mapping in tokens.json rather than duplicating color values to keep runtime switching cheap
Expose bridge tokens under tokens.bridge.* to avoid colliding with existing tokens and allow gradual migration
Charts (recharts + d3 wrappers) should fallback to tokens.bridge.grid-line then tokens.divider if missing
Tables: reuse tokens.bridge.elevated-surface for sticky header background to ensure consistent elevation logic
Performance: small alias map lookup at startup; no runtime repaint expected beyond theme swap event
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Design review and token spec merged -> Phase 2: Add aliases and update storybook (canary) -> Phase 3: Migrate two low-risk console pages -> Phase 4: Full console rollout with feature flag and opt-out for early customers. Each phase includes visual regression and accessibility checks.
